screen19-a1.description: top-left of the profile sheet over a dark banner (records call it Back
screen19-a1.visible_text: none (X glyph on the dark banner, top-left)
screen19-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Back"; talkback_label (same) — used only to know what to watch for when tapping; not used in the verdict
screen19-a1.convention_relied_on: X = close; my reading, confidence high
screen19-a1.initial_rationale: unlabeled close convention; exemption pending the tap
screen19-a1.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a1 (same control, tested once): the X closed the profile sheet, matching the convention

screen19-a2.glyph: rounded mascot face with two eyes on a blue circle
screen19-a2.visible_text: none (large round avatar with a green dot)
screen19-a2.convention_relied_on: avatar = your profile picture / view profile; my reading, confidence medium
screen19-a2.initial_rationale: unlabeled avatar; convention suggests viewing or changing the picture; exemption pending the tap
screen19-a2.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a2 (same control, tested once): the avatar changes online status, which neither the picture convention nor anything visible (only a tiny green dot) predicts
screen19-a2.recommendation: put a visible caption such as 'Status: Online' next to the dot, or make the dot itself a labeled status control

screen19-a3.description: status bubble with a plus-in-circle glyph and an italic prompt
screen19-a3.visible_text: italic prompt "Last song stuck in your head?" with a plus-in-circle glyph (wording rotates between visits)
screen19-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Add custom status"; talkback_label (same) — used only to know what to watch for when tapping; not used in the verdict
screen19-a3.initial_rationale: a question in italics does not say it sets a status; the wording changes on each visit
screen19-a3.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a3 (same control, tested once): the bubble sets a custom status but only the destination says so; its rotating question never names status
screen19-a3.recommendation: prefix a fixed label, e.g. 'Set status: What have you been reading?'

screen19-a4.description: display name with a down chevron
screen19-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Accessibility Testing"; talkback_label (same) — used only to know what to watch for when tapping; not used in the verdict
screen19-a4.initial_rationale: a name with a chevron reads as an account dropdown; nothing says what it opens
screen19-a4.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a4 (same control, tested once): the display name opens an online-status chooser; nothing on the name conveys status
screen19-a4.recommendation: show the status next to the name with a label ('Online ▾ change status') so the chevron belongs to something named

screen19-a5.description: filled button with a pencil glyph
screen19-a5.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Edit Profile"; talkback_label (same) — used only to know what to watch for when tapping; not used in the verdict
screen19-a5.initial_rationale: the words say what it does
screen19-a5.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a5 (same control, tested once): visible text names the action; no test required

screen19-a6.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Main"; talkback_label (same) — used only to know what to watch for when tapping; not used in the verdict
screen19-a6.initial_rationale: a tab paired with 'Wishlist'; switching the panel is the purpose
screen19-a6.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a6 (same control, tested once): the tab switched back to the default profile panel

screen19-a7.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a7 (same control, tested once): the tab showed a wishlist with a plain explanation of what goes in it; the everyday word held

screen19-a8.description: top-right of the 'Amp up your profile' card
screen19-a8.visible_text: none (X at the top-right of the 'Amp up your profile' card)

screen19-a8.convention_relied_on: X = dismiss/close; my reading, confidence high

screen19-a8.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a8 (same control, tested once): the X dismissed the card, as the convention promises

screen19-a9.description: button in the 'Amp up your profile' card
screen19-a9.visible_text: "Get Nitro" with a Nitro glyph, in the card 'Amp up your profile'
screen19-a9.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Get Nitro"; talkback_label (same) — used only to know what to watch for when tapping; not used in the verdict
screen19-a9.initial_rationale: 'Nitro' is a product name; nothing says it is a paid subscription
screen19-a9.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a9 (same control, tested once): the button leads to a monthly paid subscription; the label is a brand name that conveys neither the purchase nor what it buys
screen19-a9.recommendation: name the action plainly, e.g. 'Subscribe to Nitro ($9.99/month)' or 'See paid upgrades'

screen19-a10.description: button in the 'Amp up your profile' card

screen19-a10.initial_rationale: 'Shop' under 'Amp up your profile' says what it is
screen19-a10.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a10 (same control, tested once): the button opened the Shop

screen19-a11.visible_text: "Orbs Balance" (value still loading: three faint dots)
screen19-a11.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Orbs balance: Loading, busy"; talkback_label (same) — used only to know what to watch for when tapping; not used in the verdict
screen19-a11.initial_rationale: 'Orbs' is product jargon; a balance row does not say what pressing it does
screen19-a11.deciding_evidence: carried from screen7-a11 (same control, tested once): a row labeled as a balance opens a sponsored-video Quests page; 'Orbs' is never explained before the tap
screen19-a11.recommendation: say what orbs are and what the row opens, e.g. 'Orbs (reward points): 0 — earn more by watching videos'
